selections.heading: Corrections
selections.text: The Plan Approval tags belong in `code-generation-questions.md`, not in `code-generation-plan.md`. The plan's own content is bound by the approval fingerprint, so a fingerprint written into the plan changes the very value it is meant to state. the engine's `fingerprint` command only ever writes those tags into the questions file. The earlier pass had copied them into both files, which made the fingerprint permanently stale and blocked generation.

selections.heading: Corrections
selections.text: Step 4 of this stage is a conformance pass over code an earlier pass already wrote, not a greenfield implementation. `source-manifest.json` lists 23 workspace files that exist on disk and are complete, runnable implementations of most of the system.

selections.heading: Corrections
selections.text: Plan steps 15–18 were added to the plan after the initial plan was written, to close requirement gaps found while reviewing the existing code against `requirements.md` (FR1.4, FR1.5, FR4.6, FR4.7). The original plan's 14 steps already describe the same architecture. these four steps correct behaviour that already exists rather than adding new design.

selections.heading: Corrections
selections.text: The plan's `## Plan Approval` section was replaced with a pointer to the questions file instead of carrying the tags and options inline. The engine parses the approval evidence from the questions file only.

selections.heading: Corrections
selections.text: `traceability.json` was written with `reverse[]` entries shaped `{path, ids}`, but the `traceability` sensor requires every `reverse[]` entry to carry its own `id`, `status` and `target`, and requires `upstream_ids` to list every id extracted from `requirements.md` — including the `FR1`…`FR5` group headings, which the sensor's `\bFR\d+(?:\.\d+)?\b` pattern picks up from the H3 headings. The file was rewritten to that shape and the sensor passed. The stage prose shows only the `coverage[]` shape, so the `reverse[]` and `upstream_ids` requirements are only discoverable by reading `.claude/tools/aidlc-sensor-traceability.ts`.

selections.heading: Corrections
selections.text: The out-of-band reviewer process turned out to be unnecessary. Dispatching `subagent_type: general-purpose` with `model: opus` and inlining the reviewer's agent definition in the prompt works in-process: the `sonnet`/`haiku` overrides are rejected by the Agent tool's own input validation, and `opus` is accepted when it is passed to `general-purpose` rather than to the named reviewer agent. Inlining the definition keeps the agent in the architecture-reviewer role, including its required `**Reviewer:** aidlc-architecture-reviewer-agent` identity marker on the first line.

selections.heading: Corrections
selections.text: Chose a migration on the existing `assets` table for the assignment and return timestamp columns rather than redefining the table. The `poc` database may already exist on a developer machine, and a redefinition would strand it.
